description: De-AI writing skill for any Agent Skills-compatible agent (77+ via the Skills CLI), with native plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, and Antigravity. Narrative-architecture repair for fiction, venue-matched rules for professional prose. Based on StoryScope (arXiv:2604.03136).

latest_release.name: v0.13.0
latest_release.body:
A minor release. Rules that contradicted each other now have one statement each, three papers were read into the rules or the ledger, and the persona validator refuses one more token, so a private persona that lists `professional-pass.md check 8` no longer validates.

## What you will notice

- **Persona validator.** `professional-pass.md check 8` (templatedness) is refused as an override token, like check 9: everything it hunts is repetition across the piece, which stays a uniformity finding whatever a persona's table says. If your own persona lists it, drop the row (#307).
- **Report lines.** The fiction report gains `Discourse:` and `Style scan:` lines between Group E and Advisories; the professional report gains a `Discourse:` line on routes that load `discourse-pass.md`. The outline and QUD check runs by route, not by length (#303).
- **Quoted material.** Quotations are protected without being declared, whatever their source. The one exception is dialogue and documents inside invented fiction, which the passes may revise unless you declare them protected. A defect inside protected quoted material is now reported on a `Protected:` line instead of having no line. Dialect and deliberate nonstandard spelling are never regularized (#297).
- **Refactor and recreate.** Refactor adds no verdict or recommendation the source lacks, and records a missing one on `Deferred:` (#296). Recreate under a voice or persona starts from both canonical stages, the defect list (scored as refactor stage 1 is) and the verified fact list (#305).
- **Scoped runs.** When you name the files to edit, venue samples are read only if you supply them besides the target; otherwise the domain baseline applies (#296). With no target, sepia asks for one, or on an unattended run says none was given and stops (#295).
- **Journalism numbers.** Rule 4 asks for a comparison only on a figure the reader cannot size on its own, stated in the figure's unit or with the conversion written out; three slips or 14:05 need none (#302).
- **Persona check 6.** Under a persona that overrides check 6, three of its items still report as uniformity: every section the same length, lists of exactly three everywhere, and fractal summaries. Emoji, bold mini-heading lists and Title Case stay waived (#304).

## Rules from papers

- **Not X, but Y** (Peng et al. 2026, ledger `PENG-NOTX-2026`): an "it's not X, it's Y" frame may stay when it passes four checks taken from the paper's classification; a kept frame still counts toward the §3 cluster. The keep test is a Sepia inference (#299).
- **Time structure** (Raiyan et al. 2026, ledger `RAIYAN-2026`): on fiction write, set the sheet's time structure from what the story withholds, not from a named shape taken as a rule. Readers comparing two versions by the same model preferred the one written without a shape instruction in 76% of decisive judgments; nonlinearity the story motivates was not tested (#300).
- **Clark et al.** is listed under "Consulted, no rule" in the research ledger (#301).

## Evidence wording

The em dash row, the Chinese second-person row and the journalism attribution rows now state what their sources measured: the em dash rate moves with the writing condition as well as the release; second person in dialogue, an instruction or a reader-directed condition stays; a quotation is attributed by context or a plain verb, placed as the venue places it (#298).

## Housekeeping

Domain files point to `SKILL.md` Routing instead of restating their load sets; a changelog was the one place that read as exempt from the style pass (#306). The postmortem route loads `discourse-pass.md` §1–3, as its domain file already required (#295). A warning about formula endings now points to its real definition (#308).

## Not in this release

- A routing row for narrative non-fiction essays (#283). It waits on a live run against a real essay in that genre.
- A length threshold for "long professional pieces". A baseline review gave a 650-word fea

detail.readme_excerpt:
# sepia

**English** | [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![behavioral eval](https://github.com/Nanako0129/sepia/actions/workflows/behavioral-eval.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Nanako0129/sepia/actions/workflows/behavioral-eval.yml) [![version consistency](https://github.com/Nanako0129/sepia/actions/workflows/version-consistency.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Nanako0129/sepia/actions/workflows/version-consistency.yml) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Nanako0129/sepia)](https://github.com/Nanako0129/sepia/releases/latest) [![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

> De-AI writing at the layer that actually gives AI away. Fiction gets its narrative architecture repaired before anyone touches word choice; professional documents (release notes, PR replies, postmortems, tickets, technical articles) each get rules matched to their venue.

A portable [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io/specification): any agent that speaks the standard can load it, and the [Skills CLI](https://skills.sh), which supports 77+ agents, installs it with one command. Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity, and QwenPaw additionally get native plugin packaging. One canonical `SKILL.md`, no per-platform forks. Four operations: **write**, **review** (diagnose only), **refactor** (minimal edits), **recreate** (full rewrite).

## Table of Contents

- [Why another humanizer](#why-another-humanizer)
- [Operation entries](#operation-entries)
- [Experimental: composing with voice skills](#experimental-composing-with-voice-skills)
- [Sentence rhythm and Chinese calibration](#sentence-rhythm-and-chinese-calibration)
- [Install](#install)
- [Uninstall](#uninstall)
- [Layout](#layout)
- [Star History](#star-history)
- [Sources](#sources)
- [Support](#support)
- [License](#license)

---

## Why another humanizer

Every popular humanizer edits word choice and syntax. [StoryScope](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03136) (Russell et al., 2026: 61,608 stories, human + 5 frontier LLMs) showed that a classifier using **narrative-structure features alone** detects AI fiction at 93.2% macro-F1. In the same study's LAMP-edited condition, where human editors had rewritten the surface style, detection dropped only from 95.5% to 93.9%. The tells that survive are architectural: themes explained by the narrator, single-track causally-tidy plots, emotions rendered only as bodily sensation, no real-world references, no reader, linear time, endings resolved by protagonist growth and acceptance.

sepia turns those measured gaps, together with the related studies digested in [`research/`](research/), into a three-pass writing and revision protocol for fiction:

| Pass | Layer | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Narrative architecture (fiction) | stop explaining the theme, loosen the causal chain, back-load revelations, mix emotion modes, sparse character networks, name real things |
| 2 | Discourse flow | de-template the paragraph-q
